evidence: The patch applies to the base snapshot. generated/ differs from base only in docs/rules.md and three new files (engine.json, CacheClusterEngine.py, test_cache_cluster_engine.py), the same set as patch.diff. run-06/patch.diff and judge-context/patch.diff are byte-identical (cmp).
patch.diff hunk '@@ -178,6 +178,7 @@' matches base docs/rules.md:178-180 (E3639/E3641/E3647 context).
No tests were run. Static reading predicts the candidate's own test file fails on two cases (see requirement_intent), but that is a behavior finding, not an apply failure.

generated/src/cfnlint/rules/resources/elasticache/CacheClusterEngine.py sits in the same directory as the reference rule and sibling CacheClusterCacheNodeTypeEnum.py (base/src/cfnlint/rules/resources/elasticache/).
generated/src/cfnlint/data/schemas/extensions/aws_elasticache_cachecluster/engine.json sits beside cachenodetype_enum.json, matching the reference's extension directory.
generated/test/unit/rules/resources/elasticache/test_cache_cluster_engine.py matches the reference test path.
Names match the reference: id 'E3695' (generated CacheClusterEngine.py:13), class CacheClusterEngine (:12), keywords 'Resources/AWS::ElastiCache::CacheCluster/Properties' (:21).

The emitted error contract differs. generated CacheClusterEngine.py:19-26 does not pass all_matches=True, so base/src/cfnlint/rules/jsonschema/CfnLintJsonSchema.py:49-52 replaces the error message with shortdesc ('Validate ElastiCache cluster engines', via :44-45).

Reference sets all_matches=True (reference/src/cfnlint/rules/resources/elasticache/CacheClusterEngine.py:28) and its test expects raw enum messages (reference/test/unit/rules/resources/elasticache/test_cache_cluster_engine.py:70, "'oss-redis' is not one of ['memcached', 'redis', 'valkey']").
No EngineVersion error contract exists in the candidate. The reference test expects an EngineVersion enum error for redis '7.1.0' (reference test :40-46).
criteria.deficiency: The rule's error messages and coverage diverge from the reference contract. With all_matches defaulting to False, every error is reported as the shortdesc instead of the specific enum message. The rule also has no EngineVersion error path, which the reference provides.

evidence: generated CacheClusterEngine.py:8-9 imports the extension package and CfnLintJsonSchema/SchemaDetails, the same pattern as base/src/cfnlint/rules/resources/elasticache/CacheClusterCacheNodeTypeEnum.py:6-7.
No new reverse dependency is introduced.
Rules are loaded by module import (base/src/cfnlint/rules/_rules.py:180 and :370 use importlib), so no manual registration is needed. The reference also adds none.
The extension package has __init__.py (base/src/cfnlint/data/schemas/extensions/aws_elasticache_cachecluster/__init__.py), and the candidate's class and filename match its module.
The candidate adds no third-party or new internal dependencies. Its imports are cfnlint modules already used by sibling rules (generated CacheClusterEngine.py:8-9; test imports at test:6-11).

The rule class lives in the rules layer (generated CacheClusterEngine.py:12-26). The enum data lives in the schema-data layer (generated engine.json:1-13), the same split as the reference and the RDS analog.
The candidate's problem is how the data is produced, not where it lives (see extension_point_adherence).

The reference extends that script with write_elasticache_engines and elasticache_api (reference/scripts/update_schemas_from_aws_api.py), generating aws_elasticache_cachecluster/engine_version.json (reference/src/cfnlint/data/schemas/extensions/aws_elasticache_cachecluster/engine_version.json:1-129).

criteria.deficiency: The candidate bypasses the existing update-script mechanism that the RDS analog and the reference both use. The engine list is hard-coded, so it will drift from AWS data without a refresh path.

evidence: The rule uses the CfnLintJsonSchema/SchemaDetails abstraction only (generated CacheClusterEngine.py:19-26), with no direct template, transport, or persistence coupling.
Function-resolution behavior is handled by the existing validator layer, not reimplemented in the rule.

No type guard on Engine. generated engine.json:5-13 applies enum unconditionally. The repo's analog guards with if {properties:{Engine:{type:string}}, required:[Engine]} (base/src/cfnlint/data/schemas/extensions/aws_rds_dbinstance/engine_version.json:7) and so does the reference (reference/src/cfnlint/data/schemas/extensions/aws_elasticache_cachecluster/engine_version.json:7-12).
No all_matches=True. The analog base/src/cfnlint/rules/resources/rds/DbClusterEngineVersion.py:26 sets it, as does the reference (reference CacheClusterEngine.py:28).

docs/rules.md is generated and sorted by rule ID (base/src/cfnlint/maintenance.py:45-46). The candidate hand-inserts E3695 at generated/docs/rules.md:181, between E3647 (:180) and E3652 (:182), which breaks ID order. The reference does not hand-edit docs.
The candidate's test expectations contradict its own rule (generated test:41-46 and :51; see requirement_intent).
criteria.deficiency: Missing the if/type-string guard used by the RDS analog, missing all_matches=True used by the analog and reference, a hand-edited generated docs file placed out of ID order, and test expectations that disagree with the implementation.

evidence: Engine-only scope. The task title is 'Create rule E3695 to validate cache cluster engines'. The reference rule validates engine and engine version together (reference CacheClusterEngine.py description, 'Validate the Elasticache cluster engine along with the engine version'), and its schema covers EngineVersion per engine (reference engine_version.json:30-121). The candidate validates only the Engine enum (generated engine.json:5-13).

False positive on intrinsic values. generated CacheClusterEngine.py:19-26 calls the base validate path, and base/src/cfnlint/rules/jsonschema/CfnLintJsonSchema.py:69-81 sets context functions=[]. base/src/cfnlint/jsonschema/_filter.py:128-130 then passes the raw dict through, and base/src/cfnlint/jsonschema/_keywords.py:209-218 rejects {'Ref': ...} against the enum. So a template with Engine: !Ref EngineParam yields an E3695 error. The reference avoids this via the type guard (reference engine_version.json:7-12).

The candidate's own test contradicts its implementation. generated test:41-46 expects [] for {'Engine': {'Ref': 'Engine'}}, but by the trace above it returns an error. generated test:47-58 expects message "'foo' is not one of ['memcached', 'redis', 'valkey']" (:51), but CfnLintJsonSchema.py:49-52 replaces it with the shortdesc, and base/src/cfnlint/jsonschema/exceptions.py:105-106 compares message in __eq__. Both cases would fail by reading.

Static prediction against the reference test (not executed): instance0, instance1, instance2 and instance5 return [] and pass. instance3 (redis, EngineVersion '7.1.0') returns [] but expects an EngineVersion error, so it fails. instance4 ('oss-redis') returns one error with the shortdesc message and schema_path ['properties','Engine','enum'], but the reference expects the raw message and ['allOf',0,'then','properties','Engine','enum'], so it fails.
criteria.deficiency: The feature is narrower than the reference (no EngineVersion validation). It also flags valid intrinsic-function engine values, and its own test file contradicts the rule's behavior. The reference-derived tests are predicted to fail on instance3 and instance4.
